all_entries.title: Circulating tumor DNA-based assessment of disease progression after liver resection or transplantation for metastatic colorectal cancer or hepatocellular carcinoma-study protocol for a randomized, controlled trial
all_entries.summary: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) monitoring is being evaluated for its clinical utility in detecting minimal residual disease (MRD) after liver resection or transplantation for metastatic colorectal cancer (CRLM) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This randomized controlled trial aims to determine if ctDNA can provide earlier detection of disease progression compared to conventional imaging and biomarkers, which have limited sensitivity.

all_entries.title: New Compass for Precision Oncology: Evidence, Challenges, and Prospects of Circulating Tumor DNA in Colorectal Cancer
all_entries.summary: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) serves as a clinically actionable biomarker in colorectal cancer management. Enhanced analytical accuracy and sequencing depth have broadened ctDNA's applications, including molecular profiling of advanced disease, postoperative risk stratification, and real-time assessment of therapeutic response and resistance. Additionally, ctDNA-based assays integrating mutation analysis and methylation are valuable in screening and early detection.

all_entries.title: Evaluation of Droplet Digital PCR Assay for the Detection of Microsatellite Instability in Colorectal, Gastric, and Endometrial Cancers
all_entries.summary: Droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was evaluated for detecting microsatellite instability (MSI) using BAT-26, ACVR2A, and DEFB105A/B markers in colorectal, gastric, and endometrial cancers. The study demonstrated that ddPCR is a highly sensitive method for MSI detection, which is crucial for diagnosing Lynch syndrome and informing immunotherapy decisions.

all_entries.title: Practical integration of ctDNA-defined minimal residual disease in gastrointestinal cancers: testing windows and evidence-aligned management frameworks
all_entries.summary: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) serves as a biomarker for minimal residual disease and tumor burden in gastrointestinal cancers, including colorectal cancer. This narrative review discusses practical testing windows, assay selection, and evidence-based management frameworks for integrating ctDNA into clinical practice. The review highlights that the strongest evidence supports ctDNA utilization in resected gastrointestinal cancers, indicating its potential role in monitoring and guiding treatment decisions.

all_entries.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Blood-Based cfDNA/ctDNA Tests for Colorectal Cancer-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
all_entries.summary: Blood-based assays for colorectal cancer screening, specifically circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA) tests, show variable diagnostic performance across different platforms. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to assess their accuracy compared to stool-based tests. The findings highlight the need for standardized methodologies to improve the reliability of these non-invasive screening modalities in clinical practice.

all_entries.title: A Neural Network-Enabled, Enzymatic cfDNA Methylation Assay for Colorectal Cancer Early Detection
all_entries.summary: A non-NGS liquid biopsy assay utilizing methylation profiling of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) was developed for early detection of colorectal cancer (CRC). The assay targets 40 CpG regions identified through bioinformatic analysis. Clinical evaluation indicates potential for improved sensitivity and scalability compared to current noninvasive screening methods, addressing limitations in early CRC detection.

all_entries.title: Successful Management of BRAF V600E-Mutated Metastatic Colorectal Cancer With Liver Dysfunction Using Encorafenib-Based Therapy
all_entries.summary: Encorafenib-based therapy, including cetuximab and FOLFOX, is established as a first-line treatment for BRAF V600E-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). This case report highlights its successful application in a patient with significant liver dysfunction, addressing a gap in safety and efficacy data for this population often excluded from clinical trials.

all_entries.title: Rapid On-Site Next-Generation Sequencing: An Alternative to Single-Gene and Send-Out Testing in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer and Colorectal Cancer in a Community Pathology Laboratory Setting
all_entries.summary: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) using the ThermoFisher Oncomine Precision Assay (OPA) was assessed as an alternative to single-gene panels and send-out NGS for identifying actionable mutations in colorectal cancer. The study focused on turnaround time, quantity not sufficient rates, and detection of NCCN-recommended alterations, indicating that OPA may enhance efficiency in mutation identification for targeted therapies in a community pathology laboratory setting.

all_entries.title: Clinical Impact of Baseline ctDNA RAS/BRAF Mutations on Conversion Surgery and Outcomes in First-Line Anti-EGFR Therapy for Advanced Colorectal Cancer
all_entries.summary: Baseline ctDNA RAS/BRAF mutations were assessed in patients with unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer undergoing first-line anti-EGFR therapy. The study indicates that the presence of these mutations may influence conversion surgery rates and overall outcomes. This highlights the importance of ctDNA testing for RAS/BRAF mutations in guiding treatment decisions and predicting surgical candidacy in advanced colorectal cancer.

all_entries.title: An exploratory multimodal pipeline for recurrence prediction in CRC with XELOX therapy
all_entries.summary: A multimodal machine learning pipeline was assessed for predicting recurrence in 86 colorectal cancer patients treated with XELOX. The study integrated clinicopathological and liquid biopsy data, identifying 17 recurrences. This exploratory research suggests that combining these data types may enhance risk stratification in CRC recurrence post-surgery and adjuvant therapy.

all_entries.title: Signals of inequity in the care pathway: rural lab diagnosis, systemic therapy delays, and RAS mutation differences in metastatic colorectal cancer
all_entries.summary: Geographic disparities affect access to biomarker testing for RAS, BRAF, and microsatellite instability (MSI) in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) patients in rural Canada. The study highlights inequities in the care pathway, suggesting that rural populations may experience delays in diagnosis and systemic therapy, potentially impacting outcomes.

all_entries.title: Neural cues differentially modulate colorectal cancer cell behavior depending on patients' genomic background
all_entries.summary: Neural cues influence colorectal cancer cell behavior variably based on genomic background, including microsatellite instability (MSI) and KRAS/BRAF mutations. In patient-derived CRC cell lines, most neural signals enhanced clonogenicity, with specific adrenergic signals showing differential effects. This suggests that the interaction between neural signals and genomic status may inform therapeutic strategies and prognostic assessments in CRC management.

all_entries.title: Absence of co-occurrence between HER2 amplification and dMMR/MSI in a large multicentric colorectal cancer cohort
all_entries.summary: In a large multicentric colorectal cancer cohort, the study found no co-occurrence between HER2 amplification and mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR)/microsatellite instability (MSI). This suggests that HER2 amplification may be mutually exclusive with dMMR/MSI, which has implications for targeted therapy and the assessment of Lynch Syndrome. The findings highlight the need for careful biomarker evaluation in CRC to guide treatment decisions.

all_entries.title: Intermuscular adipose tissue as a prognostic biomarker for overall survival in colorectal cancer
all_entries.summary: Intermuscular adipose tissue (IMAT) serves as an independent prognostic biomarker for overall survival in colorectal cancer (CRC). The IMAT model may improve prognostic accuracy and inform personalized treatment strategies for CRC patients.

all_entries.title: Who Truly Benefits from Anti-EGFR Rechallenge in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer? From Clinical Enrichment to ctDNA-Guided Molecular Hyperselection
all_entries.summary: Anti-EGFR rechallenge in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) may benefit a selected subgroup of patients who previously responded to EGFR blockade. This narrative review discusses the biological rationale, clinical evidence, and practical implementation of this strategy, emphasizing the potential for ctDNA-guided molecular hyperselection to identify optimal candidates for treatment.

all_entries.title: Investigation of a methylated BCAT1 and IKZF1 circulating tumour DNA blood test for monitoring treatment response in patients with colorectal cancer
all_entries.summary: Methylated BCAT1 and IKZF1 circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) levels correlate with treatment response in colorectal cancer patients. This biomarker testing may serve as a valuable tool for personalizing treatment strategies.

all_entries.title: Discordant Dynamics Between Absolute ctDNA and Tumor Fraction During Treatment Monitoring in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: Evidence of a Dilution Phenomenon
all_entries.summary: In metastatic colorectal cancer, tumor fraction can decrease while absolute ctDNA increases during treatment monitoring, indicating a dilution phenomenon. Simultaneous assessment of both metrics may enhance the interpretation of ctDNA dynamics, potentially informing treatment decisions.

all_entries.title: Chemotherapy for patients with circulating tumour DNA-positive, stage II colon cancer (CIRCULATE)-an AIO/ABCSG trial
all_entries.summary: In the AIO/ABCSG trial, adjuvant chemotherapy in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-positive stage II colon cancer patients did not meet the primary intention-to-treat endpoint, likely due to premature trial closure. However, per-protocol analysis indicates a potential benefit from adjuvant therapy in this subgroup, supporting the use of ctDNA testing for guiding adjuvant treatment decisions.

all_entries.title: Immune microenvironment evolution across the serrated neoplasia pathway and its relevance to immunotherapy
all_entries.summary: Serrated neoplasia pathway tumors, comprising 15%-30% of sporadic colorectal cancers, exhibit early BRAF V600E mutations and distinct immune microenvironments. Despite the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer, these tumors demonstrate significant molecular heterogeneity, impacting their response to immunotherapy. Understanding the immune microenvironment evolution in this context is crucial for optimizing treatment strategies.

all_entries.title: Clinical Applications of Liquid Biopsy in Colorectal Cancer: A Focus on Registered Clinical Trials
all_entries.summary: Liquid biopsy, analyzing tumor-derived components in blood, is being explored in colorectal cancer for early detection and patient stratification. This review assesses registered clinical trials, highlighting the potential of liquid biopsy to enhance diagnostic and follow-up strategies in CRC management.

all_entries.title: A systematic scoping review of the molecular pathogenesis of digestive system cancers (2013-2025)
all_entries.summary: Digestive system cancers (DSCs) are highly prevalent and lethal, comprising over 25% of cancer diagnoses. A systematic scoping review synthesized findings from 57 studies (2013-2025) utilizing next-generation sequencing (NGS) to identify genetic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic alterations across DSCs, including colorectal cancer. The review highlights the need for an integrated overview of molecular pathogenesis to enhance understanding and treatment strategies for these malignancies.

all_entries.title: Molecular characteristics of Chinese colorectal cancer patients with microsatellite instability
all_entries.summary: Chinese colorectal cancer patients with microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) and microsatellite stable (MSS) tumors exhibit distinct molecular characteristics, including differences in tumor mutational burden (TMB), homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) status, and driver gene alterations. This highlights the molecular heterogeneity of MSI-H colorectal cancer and suggests the necessity for future research incorporating germline and epigenetic data to enhance subtype classification.

all_entries.title: KRAS/NRAS/BRAF Mutations and Mismatch Repair Deficiency in Patients with Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: A Clinicopathological Analysis
all_entries.summary: Early-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) in young Chinese patients (ages 22-45) exhibits distinct clinicopathological features. The study analyzed 239 patients to investigate associations between these features and genetic mutations, specifically KRAS, NRAS, BRAF mutations, and mismatch repair deficiency. Key findings highlight the advanced stage at diagnosis and unique challenges in managing early-onset CRC, emphasizing the need for tailored clinical approaches based on genetic profiling.

all_entries.title: Phenotypic heterogeneity in carriers of a pathogenic MSH2 variant: implications for the diagnosis of Lynch syndrome
all_entries.summary: Carriers of a pathogenic MSH2 variant exhibit phenotypic heterogeneity, impacting Lynch syndrome diagnosis. The study highlights the importance of microsatellite instability (MSI) and immunohistochemistry (IHC) in screening algorithms for Lynch syndrome-associated tumors, which typically show MSI and loss of MMR protein expression. Understanding this heterogeneity may refine diagnostic approaches for patients with suspected Lynch syndrome.

all_entries.title: Traditional serrated adenoma of the colorectum: Evolving concepts in histological classification and terminology
all_entries.summary: Traditional serrated adenomas (TSAs) are rare colorectal polyps that often harbor KRAS or BRAF mutations, indicating distinct carcinogenic pathways. KRAS-mutant TSAs are predominantly found in the distal colorectum, while BRAF-mutant TSAs are more common proximal to the transverse colon. Understanding these mutations may aid in risk stratification and management of colorectal cancer associated with TSAs.

all_entries.title: Functional precision oncology platform of BRAF(V600E)-mutated colorectal cancer organoids predicts therapy response and reveals RNF43-mediated immunogenicity
all_entries.summary: RNF43 mutation serves as a dual biomarker for therapy sensitivity and immunogenicity in BRAF(V600E)-mutant colorectal cancer, as demonstrated by a functional precision oncology platform integrating multi-omics and immune co-culture. The study suggests that combining BRAF/EGFR inhibition with immunotherapy may enhance treatment efficacy and address drug resistance in this aggressive cancer subtype.

all_entries.title: Mismatch repair protein "nonclassic expression loss" pattern in colorectal cancer: an important staining pattern that is not well understood
all_entries.summary: Nonclassic loss of mismatch repair (MMR) proteins can occur in colorectal cancer, with 30.77% of cases exhibiting microsatellite instability high status and 3.85% associated with Lynch syndrome. This finding underscores the need for enhanced understanding of nonclassic MMR expression patterns to ensure accurate identification of patients with these conditions.

all_entries.title: Quantitation of Tucatinib, a Novel Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor in Dried Blood Spot (DBS) With LC-ESI-MS/MS: Application to a Pharmacokinetic Study in Mice
all_entries.summary: Tucatinib, a selective HER2 kinase inhibitor, was quantified in dried blood spots using LC-ESI-MS/MS in a pharmacokinetic study in mice. The study supports the use of Tucatinib as a targeted therapy for HER2-positive metastatic colorectal cancer, demonstrating its potential to improve survival and disease control, particularly in challenging cases with brain metastases.

all_entries.title: Severe renal toxicity following adjuvant envafolimab in a patient with ultra-hypermutated (POLE) stage II colorectal cancer: a case report
all_entries.summary: Ultra-hypermutated colorectal cancer (CRC) with POLE mutation may be associated with increased risk of immune-related renal toxicity following adjuvant envafolimab. This case highlights the need for careful patient selection, thorough risk-benefit assessment, and vigilant monitoring of organ function in early-stage POLE-mutated CRC patients receiving off-label immunotherapy, as the potential for unnecessary toxicity exists despite favorable prognosis.

all_entries.title: Primary Tumor-Associated Loss of the Y Chromosome and Clinical Outcome in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
all_entries.summary: Loss of the Y chromosome (LoY) is frequently observed in metastatic colorectal cancer, particularly in rectal primary tumors. The association of LoY with clinical outcomes may vary based on disease stage, molecular background, and analytical methods. These results suggest that LoY could serve as a context-dependent biomarker in colorectal cancer, warranting further investigation.

all_entries.title: Impact of Driver Genetic Alterations on Survival in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients from a Genetically Homogeneous Sardinian Population: A Real-World Study
all_entries.summary: In a real-world study of a genetically homogeneous Sardinian population with metastatic colorectal cancer, the allele frequency of RAS mutations was evaluated for its prognostic impact on survival outcomes. The findings underscore the importance of routine molecular profiling in guiding personalized treatment strategies for CRC patients.

all_entries.title: Molecular Landscape and Advanced Diagnostic Technologies for BRAF Mutations in Cancer: From Quantitative PCR and ddPCR to CRISPR-Based Platforms
all_entries.summary: BRAF mutations, particularly BRAF-V600E, are significant in colorectal cancer and other malignancies, driving MAPK pathway activation and impacting treatment response. The study discusses advanced diagnostic technologies, including quantitative PCR, ddPCR, and CRISPR-based platforms, for accurate detection of BRAF alterations, underscoring their importance in molecular classification and prognostic evaluation.

all_entries.title: Young onset rectal cancer (YORC): a descriptive tertiary center analysis
all_entries.summary: Young onset rectal cancer (YORC) is associated with more advanced disease at presentation (M+, N+, EMVI+). However, short-term survival in non-metastatic YORC patients is comparable to older patients. These findings highlight the necessity for earlier diagnosis and tailored management strategies in this demographic.

all_entries.title: Personalized pharmacotherapy of colorectal cancer
all_entries.summary: Integration of molecular biomarkers in colorectal cancer treatment facilitates personalized therapy decisions, enhancing options in both adjuvant and metastatic settings. This approach underscores the shift towards precision oncology in managing colorectal cancer.

all_entries.title: Integrated perspectives on colorectal carcinogenesis: molecular pathogenesis, genomic alterations, diagnostic paradigms, therapeutic interventions and AI-driven directions in precision oncology
all_entries.summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence is increasing, particularly among younger populations and in developing countries. This review highlights the significance of chromosomal instability (CIN), microsatellite instability (MSI), and CpG island methylation in CRC pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment strategies. It underscores the need for integrated approaches in precision oncology to address the complexities of CRC.

all_entries.title: FDG-PET/CT Parameters for distinguishing high and low microsatellite instability in colorectal cancer: A systematic review and Meta-analysis
all_entries.summary: FDG-PET/CT parameters were assessed for their ability to differentiate high microsatellite instability (MSI-H) from low microsatellite instability (MSI-L) in colorectal cancer. The systematic review and meta-analysis suggest that PET-derived metrics may provide a noninvasive alternative to traditional tissue sampling for MSI classification, potentially aiding in immunotherapy decision-making.

all_entries.title: Machine learning-based preoperative classification of colorectal cancer stage using systemic inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers
all_entries.summary: Machine learning models utilizing systemic inflammatory and nutritional biomarkers can differentiate early-stage from advanced-stage colorectal cancer preoperatively. The study suggests potential clinical utility, but emphasizes the need for larger multicenter studies with external validation to confirm these findings.

all_entries.title: RAS mutation status and immune microenvironment define distinct prognostic landscapes and predict chemotherapy benefit in pMMR colorectal cancer
all_entries.summary: RAS mutational status influences the immune microenvironment in pMMR colorectal cancer, affecting prognosis and chemotherapy response. The study suggests that combining RAS status with tumor immune microenvironment features, especially CD163, may enhance patient selection for chemotherapy benefit.
